LESSON: READING 5.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: ORAL NARRATIVES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are legends celebrated? 2. Why are some people considered heroic?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: A learner use communication and interpersonal skills to build strong and supportive ties and cultural

identity and develop a sense of belonging through reading and reflecting on the oral narratives.

● Critical thinking and problem-solving: A learner prepares and study instructions on how collecting narratives

can be conducted in the community before the project begins.

Values:
Patriotism: A learner reflects on the impact of their actions on society.

Link to other subjects:

Indigenous languages also have oral narratives, and thus, learning experiences can be shared.
